caption: The drawing depicts a wrought iron gate and two detailed sections of the ironwork, rendered in shades of brown and black. The main object is a tall, vertically oriented gate with twelve vertical bars and two horizontal bars—one near the top and one near the bottom—both of which are slightly curved, giving the gate a three-dimensional appearance. Decorative scrollwork elements are present at regular intervals along the bars, including the corners and the central section, and a symmetric finial crowns the top center. Above and to the left of the gate, there are two enlarged cross-sections of the ironwork showing close-up details: one of a vertical bar intersecting with a scroll ornament, and another of the intersection with a horizontal bar, both featuring the same ornate scrolling pattern seen on the main gate. The artist’s signature, “Geoffrey Holt,” along with the name “Harry W. Winkel,” appears in the lower right corner of the drawing. The background is a plain, off-white color, and the drawing is centered on the page with ample blank space surrounding the objects.
title: Iron Grille at Window: Restoration Drawing
cluster: #12 — Spanish Colonial Art of the Southwest
